title: BAUER GROUP RPI Image Variant Config
description: Declarative configuration for a CustomPiOS-based Raspberry Pi image. String values may reference environment variables using ${VAR} or ${VAR:-default}.

extends.description: Relative path to a parent variant JSON. This variant is deep-merged onto the parent before schema validation (objects merge, arrays concatenate).

base_image.description: Upstream image the build starts from. Must be a Raspberry Pi OS *Lite* image: this is a headless appliance (no GUI is configured anywhere), and the Desktop edition costs ~3 GiB of rootfs, which pushes the produced image past the ~7.28 GiB usable on a nominally 8 GB CM4 eMMC.

url.description: Direct .img.xz URL. `format: uri` is not enforced (generate.py validates without a format_checker), so the scheme is asserted with a pattern instead.

Raspberry Pi OS downloads must come from a raspios_lite_* directory. The Desktop (stage4) and Full (stage5) trees differ from Lite by one path segment, which is exactly how the oversized image shipped through v0.4.4.

core_freq_fixed.description: Emits core_freq_fixed=1, which disables active scaling of the core clock and pins it to the board's own turbo frequency. Upstream recommends this over per-model core_freq/core_freq_min because it is portable across Pi 4, CM4, Pi 5 and CM5. Needed when driving SPI peripherals with a hard clock ceiling (e.g. MCP2515): spi-bcm2835 computes its divisor once at probe and never revisits it, so a scaling core silently changes the real SCK. Not overclocking.

id.description: Disambiguator used ONLY as the merge key when a child variant extends a parent; never rendered. Needed when one overlay is loaded more than once, which is how the MCP251XFD family works: mcp2515 ships one overlay per channel (mcp2515-can0 / mcp2515-can1), but mcp251xfd ships ONE overlay for every channel and picks the chip with a boolean spi<n>-<m> parameter. Two entries both named 'mcp251xfd' merge by name into a single overlay carrying both chip-select selectors, with 'interrupt' resolved last-wins - one CAN interface instead of two, bound to the other channel's INT GPIO, with nothing failing at build time. Omit it and the merge key stays 'name', which is what every single-instance overlay wants.

params.description: Rendered as comma-separated dtoverlay parameters. A boolean true renders as a BARE token (dtoverlay=mcp251xfd,spi0-0) because the firmware treats overlay booleans as present-is-true/absent-is-false; false omits the key entirely, since 'k=false' would still make the parameter present.

bluetooth.description: Onboard Bluetooth radio. Enabled installs bluez and enables bluetooth.service; disabled adds dtoverlay=disable-bt and masks the service. Note that hciuart.service no longer exists on trixie - the UART attach is handled by the device tree and bluez.

enabled.description: Default true. false emits dtoverlay=disable-bt, which frees the PL011 UART for GPIO serial.

camera.description: CSI camera configuration. Pi5 always uses libcamera; Pi4 requires legacy=false (libcamera) or legacy=true (deprecated raspivid stack).

autodetect.description: camera_auto_detect=1 (Pi4/5 libcamera). Leave true unless pinning an explicit sensor overlay.

sensors.description: Explicit sensor overlays when autodetect is false (e.g. ov5647, imx219, imx296, imx378, imx477, imx519, imx708).

legacy.description: Pi4 only: start_x=1 + gpu_mem split for the deprecated raspivid stack.

hdmi.description: Per-output HDMI configuration. port 0 is the left/micro-HDMI on Pi4/5, port 1 is the right one.

force_hotplug.description: hdmi_force_hotplug - keep the port active even without a connected display.

mode.description: hdmi_mode within the chosen group (see Raspberry Pi docs for the mode table).

drive.description: hdmi_drive: hdmi routes audio, dvi does not.

audio.description: Force HDMI audio even if EDID reports none (hdmi_drive=2 + hdmi_ignore_edid_audio).

display.description: Console / DSI-LCD display settings orthogonal to HDMI.

console_rotate.description: fbcon rotation for the Linux text console.

lcd_rotate.description: display_lcd_rotate - applies to the official Pi touch DSI display.

audio.description: Audio subsystem - which output the ALSA default device lands on and whether onboard audio is active.

gpio.description: GPIO-level hardware toggles. The 1-Wire protocol is exposed as its own block for convenience (DS18B20 temperature sensors etc.).

rtc.description: I2C real-time clock HAT. A hardware RTC keeps time across power cycles on off-grid / field devices without NTP. fake_hwclock is installed as a fallback when the HAT is absent.

model.description: dtoverlay name; matches i2c-rtc's accepted values.

fake_hwclock.description: Install fake-hwclock to persist time across reboots when no HAT is attached.

fan.description: Active cooling. mode=gpio drives a simple on/off MOSFET via dtoverlay gpio-fan; mode=pwm uses the pwm-fan overlay with temp-curve; mode=emc2301 targets the Pi5 cooling HAT (built-in on the Active Cooler).

gpio.description: BCM pin for gpio/pwm fan (typically 14 on PoE HAT, 18 for PWM HAT).

leds.description: Power / activity LED behaviour. Use 'off' for stealth deployments, 'heartbeat' for liveness, 'mmc0' for disk I/O feedback.

overclock.description: Performance tuning. Requires an explicit warranty-void acknowledgement - otherwise the config fails validation.

accept_warranty_void.description: MUST be true when enabled=true. Overclocking sets the permanent OTP warranty bit on Pi4/5.

over_voltage.description: CPU/GPU core voltage offset (0.025 V steps).

memory.description: Memory split between VideoCore and Linux. Headless images should shrink gpu_mem (default 76 / 128 depending on board) to free RAM.

gpu_mem.description: Generic gpu_mem in MiB (applies to all boards unless a size-specific override is set).

cma.description: Contiguous memory allocator size (MiB). Used for camera + GL.

pcie.description: Pi5 / CM4 / CM5 PCIe slot. nvme_boot flips bootloader boot_order so the device boots from an attached NVMe first.

gen.description: Max PCIe generation (gen3 requires explicit opt-in - beyond spec but usually works on good boards).

nvme_boot.description: Advisory only - documents that the board is meant to boot from NVMe. It emits nothing on its own; the EEPROM change is made by bootloader.boot_order (e.g. 0xf461 = NVMe,USB,SD,repeat).

max_usb_current.description: Pi4 only: raise the USB port current ceiling when using a 3A supply (max_usb_current=1).

bootloader.description: Pi5 / CM5 EEPROM bootloader settings. Applied on first boot via rpi-eeprom-config.

power_off_on_halt.description: POWER_OFF_ON_HALT - actually cut power on `poweroff` instead of idling the SoC.

watchdog.description: Hardware watchdog (bcm2835-wdt). systemd kicks it automatically; failure to kick within timeout forces a reboot.

runtime_sec.description: systemd RuntimeWatchdogSec: the hardware timeout, kicked by PID 1 once per main-loop iteration and at least every timeout/2. The maximum of 15 is not a clamp boundary, it is a cliff. bcm2835_wdt_start() arms the hardware with (t << 16) & 0xfffff, so only the low four bits of the seconds survive and the effective timeout is t MOD 16: 20 gives 4s, 30 gives 14s, and 16 gives ZERO - a reset loop at every boot. Since the 6.8 fix backported into rpi-6.1.y (f33f5b1fd1be) the ioctl no longer returns EINVAL either, so an out-of-range value is applied silently and the device just reboots forever. Trixie ships exactly those kernels. Note also that PID 1 is the ONLY thing kicking below 16s (the kernel keepalive worker needs a timeout above max_hw_heartbeat_ms), and systemd issue 7932 measured 4.3s of PID 1 blocked in one SIGCHLD dispatch under a fork storm - which a Docker host with container healthchecks produces routinely. Prefer 15: it buys the largest margin the hardware allows.

reboot_sec.description: systemd RebootWatchdogSec. NOT the time allowed for an orderly shutdown - that is the natural reading and the wrong one. It arms the watchdog only for the SECOND phase of a reboot, after PID 1 has been replaced by systemd-shutdown; stopping Docker and its containers happens in phase one, governed by runtime_sec and the units' own TimeoutStopSec. Phase two runs sync_with_progress() (effectively unbounded - it resets its own attempt counter while dirty pages keep shrinking), then SIGTERM with a 90s timeout, then SIGKILL with another 90s, and only THEN issues its first watchdog_ping(): 210s worst case, open-ended. The 240 floor exists so no value can be set inside that window, where the watchdog fires during unmount_all() and corrupts the filesystem it was installed to protect. Upstream defaults to 600 and so do we.

sample_point.description: Sample point in PERCENT (e.g. 87.5) - NOT the fraction 0.875 that 'ip -details link show' prints. Rendered into 40-<name>.network as [CAN] SamplePoint=<v>%. systemd parses this key with parse_permille(), which requires a % suffix and accepts at most one decimal place; the value is rounded to one decimal on render. The 50 lower bound catches the fraction 0.875 at build time: it would otherwise render as SamplePoint=0.9%, which systemd accepts as 9 permille and the kernel then refuses (can_calc_bittiming finds no candidate with sample_point <= 9 and returns -EINVAL), leaving a device that boots with a dead CAN link. The kernel treats this value as a target and rounds DOWN to the nearest achievable point without reporting the difference. Unset lets the kernel pick, which is 87.5% at 500 kbit/s and below.

txqueuelen.description: Rendered into 70-<name>.link as TransmitQueueLength (a .link key applied by systemd-udevd, NOT a .network key). Unset leaves the CAN core default of 10.

restart_ms.description: Milliseconds after a bus-off before the controller rejoins the bus, rendered into 40-<name>.network as [CAN] RestartSec=<n>ms. Unset takes the house default of 100. 0 means no automatic recovery - the kernel and systemd default, which leaves a bus-off link dead until someone cycles it by hand.

dbitrate.description: CAN FD DATA-phase bitrate in bit/s. Setting it turns the interface into a CAN FD interface: the renderer emits [CAN] FDMode=yes alongside DataBitRate=, and the two are inseparable. can_validate() in drivers/net/can/dev/netlink.c rejects IFLA_CAN_DATA_BITTIMING without CAN_CTRLMODE_FD with -EOPNOTSUPP, and that error kills the WHOLE netlink message - the nominal bitrate, the sample point and the restart time are all lost with it, so a half-configured FD interface is not a degraded link but an unconfigured one. Requires a controller that actually does FD (MCP2518FD yes, MCP2515 no); the arbitration phase keeps using `bitrate`. Omit for classic CAN.

data_sample_point.description: CAN FD data-phase sample point in PERCENT, rendered as [CAN] DataSamplePoint=<v>%. Same parse_permille() rules and the same fraction-vs-percent trap as sample_point, and likewise ignored by systemd unless dbitrate is set (networkd only copies it into the bittiming struct inside the can_data_bitrate > 0 branch). LEAVE IT UNSET unless every node on the bus is documented to use a specific value - the sample point is a property of the bus that all nodes must agree on, not a per-board tuning knob, and the kernel already picks a sane one per bitrate in can_update_sample_point(): 75% above 800 kbit/s, 80% above 500 kbit/s, 87.5% at or below 500 kbit/s. So a 2 Mbit/s data phase defaults to 75% and a 500 kbit/s arbitration phase to 87.5% with nothing set at all.

fd_non_iso.description: Emits [CAN] FDNonISO=yes, selecting the pre-standard Bosch CAN FD frame format (different CRC and stuff-bit counter) instead of ISO 11898-1:2015. Needed ONLY to talk to first-generation FD silicon that predates the ISO standard, and the two formats do not interoperate: a non-ISO node on an ISO bus produces CRC errors, not silence. Leave unset unless a device on the bus is documented as non-ISO.

ssh.description: SSH service policy. Detailed auth settings stay under `root.ssh_*`.

banner.description: Pre-login banners (/etc/issue, /etc/issue.net) + post-login MOTD showing variant, hostname, IPv4/IPv6, CAN, docker + update status.

pre_login_note.description: Optional line appended to /etc/issue(.net), e.g. legal notice.

unattended_upgrades.description: Unattended security/system updates with configurable maintenance window and reboot policy.

allowed_origins.description: APT origin patterns to auto-upgrade (supports ${distro_id} / ${distro_codename} placeholders resolved by unattended-upgrades).

schedule.description: Maintenance window during which unattended-upgrades runs. Implemented via systemd timer override with RandomizedDelaySec.

start.description: Window start HH:MM (24h, server local time).

end.description: Window end HH:MM (24h, server local time). Run fires at a random point in [start,end].

persistent.description: If true, missed runs (e.g. offline) execute on next boot.

window.description: Reboot is only issued when current time is within this window AND a reboot is required.
